facts.value: Tradition holds that Teddy Roosevelt and his son stole the two stone lions at the door from outside a Nairobi mosque after a night out. A Nation columnist doubts it, noting the plinths say Sir John Harrington gave them.
facts.quote: stolen from outside a mosque on Government Road (now Moi Avenue) by Teddy Roosevelt and his son

facts.value: The story goes that Sir Northrup McMillan's coffin kept sticking in the mud on the way up Ol Donyo Sabuk, so Lady McMillan had him buried about halfway up.
facts.quote: The vehicle carrying the coffin up the mountain kept getting stuck in the mud. Eventually, only about half way up, Lady McMillan said

facts.value: McMillan kept a pet lion on his Juja farm and hunted many others.

facts.value: Library development in colonial Kenya followed racial lines. McMillan served Europeans only. Mombasa's Seif Bin Salim library and Nairobi's Desai Memorial Library, founded in 1942, were for Arabs and Asians respectively.
